content.value_statement: Meeting notes often miss decisions, owners, and follow-up context. This skill turns discussion text into structured notes with decisions, tasks, and next steps.
actual_capabilities: Builds standard meeting notes with agenda, attendees, discussion, decisions, questions, and follow-up items.
Extracts action items with owners, due dates, priority, dependencies, and acceptance criteria.
Formats notes for standups, sprint planning, retrospectives, decision logs, and Q&A sections.
Creates concise summaries that preserve rationale, context, metrics, and unresolved questions.
Suggests sharing, archiving, and project tracking practices for follow-through.
limitations: Requires meeting text or clear notes from the user; it does not record audio.
Cannot verify external links, attendance, decisions, or task completion without provided evidence.
May need user review before sending notes to stakeholders.
Does not update Jira, calendars, or documents unless another tool handles those actions.

use_cases.title: Convert Planning Meetings
use_cases.description: Turn sprint or project planning discussions into agenda notes, decisions, commitments, and prioritized action items.

use_cases.title: Maintain Decision Records
use_cases.description: Capture what was decided, why it mattered, who owns the next step, and what follow-up is needed.

use_cases.title: Summarize Team Rituals
use_cases.description: Create consistent notes for standups, retrospectives, reviews, and follow-up meetings across a team.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Meeting Notes
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when you have rough notes from a meeting.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create clear meeting notes from this text. Include attendees, agenda, discussion summary, decisions, action items, questions, and follow-up items: [paste notes]

prompt_templates.title: Standup Summary
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for daily or asynchronous status updates.
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn these standup updates into a concise summary. Group completed work, current work, blockers, owners, and needed follow-up: [paste updates]

prompt_templates.title: Decision Log
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when decisions and rationale are the main deliverable.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a decision log from this discussion. Capture each decision, rationale, owner, impact, alternatives, and next step: [paste discussion]

prompt_templates.title: Stakeholder-Ready Notes
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for long meetings that need a polished summary.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this meeting transcript and produce stakeholder-ready notes. Separate context, decisions, risks, action items, unresolved questions, and parking lot items: [paste transcript]

output_examples.input: A project planning meeting with scope changes, delivery risks, and several owners.
output: Summary: The team reduced launch scope to protect the delivery date.
Decision: Move advanced filtering to the next sprint because testing capacity is limited.
Action item: Alice confirms the revised scope by Friday. Bob updates backend estimates by Tuesday.

output_examples.input: A retrospective with team feedback, quality concerns, and process experiments.
output: What worked: Faster reviews and strong collaboration on the payment feature.
What needs attention: Scope changes and staging gaps affected quality.
Next experiment: Add a scope freeze after day three and review results for two sprints.

output_examples.input: A decision-heavy meeting about security fixes and performance work.
output: Decision: Prioritize authentication rate limiting before new feature work.
Rationale: The risk is high and the fix is small enough for the current sprint.
Follow-up: Security and backend owners review completion before the next planning session.

best_practices: Provide attendee names, dates, agenda items, and known deadlines before asking for notes.
Review owners and due dates before sharing notes with a wider audience.
Ask for separate sections when decisions, risks, and parking lot items matter.
anti_patterns: Do not paste confidential transcripts unless your workspace policy allows that data.
Do not ask the skill to invent owners, deadlines, or decisions that were not discussed.
Do not publish notes without checking sensitive details and stakeholder accuracy.

faq.question: Does this skill record meetings?
faq.answer: No. It organizes text you provide. Use a separate transcription or recording tool if needed.

faq.question: Can it create action items?
faq.answer: Yes. It extracts tasks with owners, deadlines, priorities, dependencies, and acceptance criteria when details are available.

faq.question: Can it handle sprint planning and retrospectives?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes templates for planning, standups, retrospectives, decision logs, and standard meetings.

faq.question: Will it update Jira or documents automatically?
faq.answer: No. It can prepare structured notes, but integrations must be handled by other tools.

faq.question: Should I review the output?
faq.answer: Yes. Verify names, dates, decisions, and sensitive content before sharing.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
